India Reaches 300 GW Non-Fossil Capacity

India has achieved 300 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity, which is 60% of its 2030 target. The growth is driven by an increase in solar capacity. The country has surpassed a significant milestone in its transition to clean energy. The solar capacity has skyrocketed, contributing to the overall growth in non-fossil fuel capacity. The government had set a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030. The current achievement is a significant step towards meeting this target.
